title: India's DGFT proposes RCMC exemption for small export consignments
summary:
India's DGFT has proposed exempting export consignments with an FOB value of up to ₹10,000 from the requirement to obtain an RCMC under the Foreign Trade Policy 2023.
It aims to promote small-value exports through postal and courier channels by reducing compliance costs for MSMEs, artisans and D2C brands.
It will not apply to restricted goods, and stakeholders have been invited to submit comments.

title: British International Investment unveils 2026-2031 Bangladesh strategy
summary:
British International Investment (BII) has launched its 2026-2031 strategy in Bangladesh, reaffirming its long-term commitment to supporting sustainable and inclusive economic growth in the country. 
The strategy will build on its past track record by partnering with businesses to create more jobs, strengthen economic resilience, advance gender inclusion and support transition to a greener economy.

title: ICE cotton extends gains for second day on higher crude oil
summary:
ICE cotton futures extended gains for a second consecutive session, with the December 2026 contract settling 1.90 per cent higher at 80.42 cents per pound.
Stronger crude oil prices, successful Chinese state cotton reserve auctions and delayed cotton planting in India supported prices.
However, the rally came on the lightest trading volume of 2026, indicating mainly short covering.

title: Turkiye seeks deeper EU integration through customs, SEPA reforms
summary:
Turkiye Exporters Assembly chief Mustafa Gultepe recently said upgrading the nearly three-decade-old Customs Union (EUCU), joining the ‘Made in EU’ framework, and securing participation in the Single Euro Payments Area would significantly strengthen the country’s economic integration with the EU.
EU trade pacts with third countries should not lead to any disadvantage for Turkiye due to the EUCU, he noted.

title: US, Jordan strengthen trade ties with reciprocal agreement
summary:
The United States and Jordan have signed the US-Jordan Agreement on Reciprocal Trade to expand market access, reduce tariff and non-tariff barriers and strengthen supply chain resilience. 
Jordan will continue duty-free access for almost all US goods while enhancing labour, environmental and intellectual property standards.
The agreement also deepens co-operation on investment security.

title: US' Sun Chemical to debut Xennia Ruby inks at Febratex 2026
summary:
Sun Chemical will debut its Xennia Ruby acid inks in Brazil at Febratex 2026 while showcasing upgraded pigment, reactive, sublimation and DTF ink solutions.
The portfolio focuses on higher colour strength, improved fastness, process efficiency and compliance with leading sustainability standards, reinforcing the company's digital textile printing strategy in Latin America.

title: Trident's ₹100 cr innovation push redefines home textiles
summary:
Trident invested ₹100+ crore (~$12 million+) in R&D, backed by 17+ patents and 147 trademarks, strengthening India's home-textile innovation.
FY26 EBITDA margins ranged from 9.1 per cent (Welspun) to 21.1 per cent (Himatsingka), highlighting profitability as a key differentiator.
Lower US tariffs and duty-free access to the EU and UK improve FY27 export prospects.

title: Weekly price shock alert: PFY (DTY & POY) - week ended July 17
summary:
India's DTY rose 3.15 per cent, outpacing China's 1.38 per cent gain as rupee weakness and QCO enforcement enabled full cost pass-through, while Pakistan stayed flat. 
India and China reached rare DTY price parity at ~$1.36/kg despite contrasting domestic market dynamics. 
Crude surged 12–14 per cent, but weak textile demand and lower MEG prices limited cost pass-through across Asia's polyester chain.

title: Jordan invites US apparel firms to explore investment opportunities
summary:
Jordanian Minister of Industry, Trade and Supply Yarub Qudah recently discussed with American Apparel and Footwear Association (AAFA) representatives strengthening trade cooperation and exploring opportunities to attract new investments to Jordan. 
The discussions took place in Washington during a session hosted by AAFA. 
Qudah invited US companies to explore investment opportunities in Jordan.

title: Nepalese PM takes steps to revive garment industry
summary:
Following a recent meeting with representatives from the Garment Association Nepal, PM Balendra Shah has instructed ministries to clear pending administrative delays, form a dedicated Textile and Clothing Development Council and restart factories closed for long. 
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has been asked to resolve laboratory testing hurdles that have restricted exports to the US.

title: UV-resistant and fan-powered: India's next performance fabric frontier
summary:
Zeel Climate Clothing has shown summer apparel prototypes at Bharat Tex 2026 using UV-resistant, heat-resistant and moisture-absorbent synthetic fabric with fan-assisted air circulation.
The India-focused launch signals growing demand for functional fashion as heatwaves reshape clothing needs.
Zeel is selling direct-to-consumer first, with scale-up planned after consumer response data.

title: New Zealand apparel imports fall to $603 mn in H1 2026
summary:
New Zealand's apparel imports fell 3.2 per cent year on year to NZ$1.03 billion (~$603.5 million) in January-June 2026, reflecting cautious consumer demand and disciplined retailer inventories, despite a modest recovery in June.
Meanwhile, apparel exports rose 5.8 per cent in the first half and 28.9 per cent in June, driven mainly by strong growth in knitted apparel exports.

title: Canada Goose achieves 50% emissions reduction milestone
summary:
Canada Goose has completed its first five-year sustainability strategy, cutting market-based Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions by 50% from its FY19 baseline and securing SBTi-approved climate targets. 
In FY26, it diverted 100% of global warranty waste from landfill, expanded circularity and responsible sourcing, and outlined new priorities on climate action, transparency and sustainability.

title: Bangladesh’s $38.7 bn apparel exports hide 151 factory closures
summary:
Bangladesh’s RMG exports fell 1.64 per cent to $38.70 billion in FY2025-26, masking sharper mid-year weakness.
Official and association data identify 151 textile-apparel factory closures amid wider industrial exits.
TexPro data points to product and market churn rather than a major concentration shock.
New units are opening, but worker absorption remains uneven.

title: China’s apparel decline hides its grip on the textile supply chain
summary:
TexPro data show China’s apparel exports rose just 3.2 per cent in June 2026, behind 12.2 per cent growth in textiles and 27 per cent in goods exports.
First-half textile exports reached $73 billion, while apparel slipped 0.7 per cent to $72.96 billion.
Sourcing shifts may move sewing across Asia, but Chinese yarn and fabric inputs remain central.

title: 54% of tested tops fail EU fibre checks in $68 bn trade
summary:
EU tests found incorrect fibre labelling on 37 per cent of garments, with blended fabrics showing the highest failure rates. 
TexPro data place the greatest commercial exposure in the $68.43 billion tops market. 
As Digital Product Passports and EPR rules advance, verified fibre data will become critical for compliance, recycling, traceability and market access.

title: UK study to examine microplastic impact of counterfeit football shirts
summary:
University of Portsmouth researchers are launching the first study into environmental impacts of counterfeit football shirts.
The UK Intellectual Property Office-funded work will compare authentic and fake kits for microplastic shedding, carbon impact and disposal.
Findings are intended to guide brands, policymakers and environmental groups on enforcement, consumer messaging and textile-waste.

title: UK clothing exports increase 9.5% in May 2026
summary:
The UK's clothing exports rose 9.54 per cent year on year to £264 million (~$356.62 million) in May 2026 and jumped 18.38 per cent from April.
However, Q1 2026 clothing exports fell 7.87 per cent year on year, while full-year 2025 exports declined 9.17 per cent, reflecting continued pressure despite the strong monthly rebound in May 2026.
